content: 1. Monitor cardiac function and symptoms of toxicity when using drugs that may prolong the QTc interval, such as lithium and ciprofloxacin. Both agents can increase the QTc interval, so caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Ciprofloxacin increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the lomitapide dose when used concomitantly. 3. Lomitapide increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Ciprofloxacin and lumefantrine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 5. Magnesium chloride decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Co-administration of ciprofloxacin with multivalent cation-containing products (e.g., antacids, supplements) can reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Use alternatives if available. 7. Magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and magnesium sulfate all decrease ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 8. Magnesium supplements can reduce ciprofloxacin absorption by forming insoluble complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 6 hours after ciprofloxacin. 9. Mavorixafor and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, so QTc monitoring is essential in patients with risk factors or when co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs. 10. Mavorixafor increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Meclofenamate and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, especially at high doses of fluoroquinolones. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Mefenamic acid and ciprofloxacin also increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Ciprofloxacin and mefloquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 14. Ciprofloxacin increases melatonin levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor melatonin effects when co-administered with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors. 15. Meloxicam and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Ciprofloxacin decreases mestranol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ciprofloxacin increases metformin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels closely, as both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported with concomitant use of quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 18. Ciprofloxacin and methadone both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 19. Ciprofloxacin increases methotrexate levels by inhibiting renal tubular transport, potentially leading to increased plasma levels and toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ciprofloxacin and methylprednisolone increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ciprofloxacin increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Elevated mexiletine concentrations may increase therapeutic and adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ciprofloxacin increases midazolam intranasal levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to higher systemic exposure and prolonged sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ciprofloxacin increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 24. Ciprofloxacin increases miglitol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels closely, as both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported with concomitant use of quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 25. Mometasone inhaled and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 27. Nabumetone and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Naproxen and ciprofloxacin also increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Ciprofloxacin increases nateglinide effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels closely, as both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported with concomitant use of quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 30. Ciprofloxacin and nilotinib both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 31. Ciprofloxacin increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Elevated olanzapine concentrations may increase the risk of adverse effects such as orthostatic hypotension or sedation. Use caution, monitor the patient, and adjust the olanzapine dosage as needed. 32. Ciprofloxacin and olodaterol inhaled both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as QT-prolonging drugs may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 33. Omeprazole decreases ciprofloxacin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with ciprofloxacin extended-release tablets slightly reduces absorption (by 20%). 34. Osilodrostat and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Osimertinib and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 36. Oxaliplatin increases ciprofloxacin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 37. Oxaprozin and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Ozanimod and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 39. Ciprofloxacin and paliperidone both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 40. Ciprofloxacin and pasireotide both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Patiromer decreases ciprofloxacin levels by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 3 hours. 42. Ciprofloxacin and pentamidine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 43. Ciprofloxacin increases pentoxifylline levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ciprofloxacin decreases phenytoin effects by an unknown mechanism. Ciprofloxacin has been reported to both increase and decrease phenytoin concentrations. Monitor phenytoin serum concentrations in patients. 45. Ciprofloxacin and pimozide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 46. Ciprofloxacin increases pioglitazone effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels closely, as both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported with concomitant use of quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 47. Piroxicam and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. The mechanism is unknown. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Polysaccharide iron decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. 49. Ponatinib increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Prednisolone and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Prednisone and ciprofloxacin also increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Pretomanid increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting OAT3. Monitor for increased adverse effects and consider dosage reduction for OAT3 substrates. 53. Ciprofloxacin and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Probenecid increases ciprofloxacin levels by interfering with renal tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Ciprofloxacin and procainamide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 56. Quetiapine and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. 57. Quinapril decreases ciprofloxacin levels by chelation. Separate doses of quinapril and oral quinolones by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ciprofloxacin and quinidine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 59. Ciprofloxacin and quinine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 60. Quizartinib and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Conduct frequent ECG monitoring if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 61. Ciprofloxacin increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
